reading.body:
Lisa McClain's AI record is mostly money: ten PAC contributions from AI and tech companies, plus five recorded votes, with no evidence any contribution changed a vote.

The contributions run from February 2025 to August 2026 and come from the largest AI-adjacent corporate PACs: Microsoft twice at $5,000 each, Google at $5,000, Amazon three times at $2,500 each, Oracle at $1,500, Palantir employees at $2,500, Anthropic at $1,000, Meta at $1,000, and Intel at $1,000. The five votes are all Yea, on suspension motions, which are typically reserved for bipartisan or uncontroversial bills. The data does not name what any of those five bills would do, so the votes cannot be read as a position on AI policy specifically.

What this record shows is that AI money reaches Congress through the same corporate PAC channels as any other industry, and that it flows to a member whose recorded AI votes are all low-controversy suspension votes. It does not show a causal link between the checks and the votes, and the page states plainly that placement in date order is not a claim of causation. The amounts are small by federal standards, between $1,000 and $5,000, which is consistent with routine PAC giving rather than a targeted influence campaign.

The record covers one member and one two-year window. It does not include contributions to other members, spending by outside groups, lobbying, or any bill text. It also cannot say whether these companies gave because of her committee assignments, because of her district, or for reasons unrelated to AI. Compute, buildings, and power do not appear in this data at all, and nothing here should be read as evidence about data center siting, electricity demand, or the physical constraints on AI scaling.
